title: Berry–Esseen bound for smooth functions
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent real random variables on it, each in $L^3(\mu)$. Suppose each has mean zero and their second moments sum to $1$. If $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is three times continuously differentiable, and $C\ge0$ satisfies $|\psi'''(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$, then
\[
\left|\int_\Omega\psi\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\right)d\mu-\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(z)\,d\gamma(z)\right|
\le \frac{1+2\sqrt{2/\pi}}{6}\,C\sum_{i=1}^n\int_\Omega|X_i|^3\,d\mu,
\]
where $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian probability measure.
hypotheses_covered: The sum of the second moments is $1$
The absolute value of the third derivative of $\psi$ is bounded by $C$ everywhere
